problem: Given the curve $r(t)=⟨\sqrt{t}\,,\,{t}^{3}+5\,,\,2t+2⟩,$ $t\in (0,\infty ),$ find all of the points at which ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $r(t)$ are parallel.

feedback.problem: Given the curve $r(t)=⟨4t-{t}^{2},{t}^{3}⟩,$ find all points at which the tangent to the curve is parallel to the vector $⟨2,1⟩.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t-{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨4-2t,3{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $⟨0\,,\,1\,,\,3⟩$ are parallel for some specific value ${t}_{0}$ of the parameter $t$ if and only if there exists a constant $c$ such that ${r}^{′}({t}_{0})=c⟨2,1⟩.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =c⟨2,1⟩ \\ ⟨4-2t,3{t}^{2}⟩ & =c⟨2,1⟩ \\ ⟨4-2t,3{t}^{2}⟩ & =⟨2c,c⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the components gives:

$$
{\begin{aligned}4-2t=2c \\ 3{t}^{2}=c\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equation, we obtain that $c=2-t.$ Substituting in the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{t}^{2} & =2-t \\ 3{t}^{2}+t-2 & =0 \\ (3t-2)(t+1) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $⟨2,1⟩$ and ${r}^{′}$ are parallel only at the points corresponding to $t=-1,\frac{2}{3}.$

Finally, since

$$
\begin{aligned}r(-1) & =⟨4(-1)-(-1)^{2},(-1)^{3}⟩=⟨-5,-1⟩ \\ r(\frac{2}{3}) & =⟨4(\frac{2}{3})-{(\frac{2}{3})}^{2},{(\frac{2}{3})}^{3}⟩=⟨\frac{20}{9},\frac{8}{27}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

we conclude that $⟨2,1⟩$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are parallel at the points $(-5,-1)$ and $(\frac{20}{9},\frac{8}{27}).$
